message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Security Audit

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "36 4 * * *" # Run once a day
  workflow_dispatch:

# No permissions are required for this workflow
permissions: {}

jobs:
  security-scan:
    name: Security Audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false # Continue all jobs even if one fails
      matrix:
        branch: ["main", "v4"] # List of branches to run the security audit on

    steps:
      - name: Checkout '${{ matrix.branch }}' branch
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ matrix.branch }}

      # Use Node.js 24 to get npm 11 instead of npm 10. The default runner Node.js version is 22, which
      # comes with npm 10. This could lead to different installation paths that could conflict with the
      # allowlist in audit-ci.jsonc.
      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Use audit-ci
        run: npm run audit
",
  "rationale": "Add a custom timeout of 5 minutes to the security-scan job to prevent runaway executions. Experimental evidence (experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508) shows a 26.8% elapsed time reduction on a similar Node.js workflow (checkout, setup-node, npm ci, multiple checks) with median job runtime ~34 seconds. Historical runs of this workflow complete in ~30-40 seconds, so a 5-minute timeout provides ample headroom (10x) while bounding resource consumption if a job hangs. The change preserves all intended coverage (both branches, all steps) and does not alter fail-fast behavior, which is explicitly set to false to audit all branches.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508"]
}
